overview: The Medford School Committee is the governing body for Medford Public Schools, responsible for district policy, administrative oversight, labor agreements, facility planning, and annual budget approval. Over the span of 175 meetings from April 2020 through October 2026, the committee managed the COVID-19 pandemic response, addressed high school safety and climate reviews, conducted searches for executive leadership, and oversaw long-term capital repair projects. Most recently, the committee selected a geothermal HVAC system for Missituck Elementary School, approved a Construction Manager at Risk model for Roberts Elementary School repairs, and reviewed first-quarter financial and after-school programming reports.

threads.name: Medford High School building project and MSBA pipeline
threads.summary: The committee initiated efforts to address aging infrastructure at Medford High School by authorizing Massachusetts School Building Authority (MSBA) Statement of Interest submissions and establishing educational visioning goals (M30#18, M39#3, M66#6). The district was formally accepted into the MSBA Core Program eligibility phase, leading the committee to establish the Medford Comprehensive High School Building Committee and define its voting composition (M85#5, M89#5, M90#5). The committee hired Left Field as Owner's Project Manager and narrowed potential building sites, navigating a historic DCR deed restriction on Edgerly Field that altered design options (M134#5, M139#6, M160#3, M163#2). Educational plans were approved, and community forums were held as the body moved toward selecting a preferred schematic design (M151#3, M166#4, M168#7).

threads.name: School building facilities, HVAC upgrades, and capital repairs
threads.summary: Over multiple terms, the committee managed urgent capital maintenance across aging facilities, addressing classroom roof leaks, hot water systems, and widespread HVAC failures (M11#12, M25#6, M77#6). Major decarbonization and HVAC replacement projects were authorized for Andrews and McGlynn middle schools alongside City Council bond approvals (M97#6, M122#6, M131#7). The body established capital planning policies and evaluated district-wide facilities condition assessments identifying priority repair needs (M103#9, M145#3, M148#6). Capital projects expanded to elementary facilities, culminating in decisions to select geothermal systems for Missituck Elementary and a Construction Manager at Risk model for Roberts Elementary repairs (M129#1, M171#4, M175#4, M175#5).

threads.name: Superintendent leadership search, evaluation, and transition
threads.summary: The committee conducted annual goal setting and performance evaluations for Superintendent Dr. Marice Edouard-Vincent throughout her contract extension (M05#12, M14#6, M20#1, M71#6, M74#2). Following Superintendent Edouard-Vincent's announced departure, the committee appointed Assistant Superintendent Dr. Suzanne Galusi as Interim Superintendent and approved her contract and transitional goals (M121#2, M123#3, M124#2). After evaluating Dr. Galusi's performance during her interim tenure, the committee voted to appoint her as permanent Superintendent and executed a three-year employment contract (M150#6, M151#4, M161#6).

threads.name: District operating budget, supplemental funding, and fiscal planning
threads.summary: The committee navigated annual operating budget cycles, combining ESSER pandemic relief funds and municipal appropriations to support district operations (M15#7, M20#2, M74#4). Mid-year shortfalls in FY24 prompted financial remediation plans, structural corrections, and the appointment of new finance leadership (M89#4, M92#5, M104#1). Following voter approval of local ballot override questions, the committee passed supplemental budget appropriations to restore cut positions and fund collective bargaining reserves (M110#8, M118#7, M123#7). The committee continued revising budget calendars and engaging in joint fiscal planning with city officials to address rising fixed costs (M155#5, M156#3, M168#4).

threads.name: High school safety, culture assessments, and student discipline
threads.summary: Rising behavioral concerns and a December 2022 stabbing at Medford High School prompted emergency public safety sessions and 10-point safety action plans (M27#4, M58#4, M59#5). The committee commissioned an independent culture, climate, and safety assessment by consultant Michael Welch, leading to policy updates on hallway monitoring, dress codes, and cell phone usage (M59#6, M68#7, M78#4). Disciplinary reporting protocols and restorative justice practices were reviewed to track out-of-school suspensions and subgroup disproportionality (M32#5, M56#11, M92#12, M97#7). Safety monitoring technology was continuously expanded across secondary buildings, including vape detectors and security camera upgrades (M88#8, M120#9, M153#5).

threads.name: Elementary school overcrowding, space utilization, and redistricting
threads.summary: Surging enrollment at Roberts Elementary School led to capacity concerns, prompts for redistricting, and space utilization studies across elementary facilities (M28#5, M108#8, M109#6). The committee evaluated proposals from facility utilization studies, including grade reconfiguration options such as K-4 and 5-6 models (M146#5, M147#5). Short-term space relief was approved by relocating Medford Early Education Program (MEEP) preschool classrooms from Roberts to Missituk Elementary (M137#6). The committee subsequently voted to delay potential middle school grade reconfiguration changes to 2028 while refining intra-district transfer guidelines and elementary reassignment policies (M170#4, M174#5).

threads.name: Before and after school care program expansion and tuition policy
threads.summary: High demand and persistent waitlists for school-age childcare led the committee to authorize seat expansions, wage adjustments, and sliding-scale tuition structures (M14#9, M29#9, M57#4). The committee replaced traditional waitlists with an on-demand lottery system for incoming kindergartners and established rate adjustments for summer and school-year programs (M64#5, M66#8, M91#7). To resolve ongoing capacity constraints, the body engaged the Belmont After School Enrichment Collaborative (BASIC) for program consulting and approved structural expansions with full-time site directors (M135#2, M161#4). Operational updates showed a 50 percent increase in program enrollment and significant waitlist reductions (M172#5, M175#3).

threads.name: Labor relations and collective bargaining agreements
threads.summary: The committee conducted regular executive sessions and open-session votes to negotiate and ratify contracts across district bargaining units, including paraprofessionals, nurses, administrators, custodians, and cafeteria workers (M09#1, M49#1, M51#2, M102#2, M103#2). Negotiations with the Medford Teachers Association involved public impasse declarations, state mediation, and eventual multi-year contract ratifications (M48#5, M52#4, M58#5, M133#3). The committee ratified subsequent agreements for nurses, paraprofessionals, administrators, and custodians while adjusting staff duty structures and extending the school day (M136#6, M140#2, M142#1, M150#2).
